journey.name: Restore — an encrypted recovery file
journey.description:
The other restore door, for someone who saved a `recovery.pkarr` rather than writing words down.
The interesting failure is a **wrong passphrase**, which must never be reported as "no account": a failed decryption says nothing at all about whether the account exists, and confusing the two sends someone hunting for a lost identity over a typo.
The file format matters and is easy to get wrong invisibly. A recovery file on disk is raw bytes; the FFI works in Base64. A file Loopky writes must be openable by pubky.app and Pubky Ring, and vice versa — so the cross-app check at the end is the real test.

actions.action: From a signed-out Loopky, tap "onboarding_restore", then "restore_method_file"
Tap "restore_file_choose" and pick a file that is NOT a recovery file (a photo). Verify "restore_outcome_title" reads "Couldn't read that file" — the size cap rejects it before it is read into memory
Pick a real recovery.pkarr, enter the WRONG passphrase, and submit
Verify the outcome reads "That didn't open the file" and explicitly does NOT claim the account is missing
Verify logcat shows no "lookupHomeserver:" line for that attempt — a file that will not open has nothing to look up
Enter the correct passphrase and submit. Verify Loopky lands on home
Settings → verify the homeserver row is populated, not "Unknown" — the session payload carries no homeserver, so it has to be resolved
Verify the backup screen does NOT offer a recovery phrase for this account ("backup_method_phrase" absent): BIP-39 runs one way, so a file-restored key genuinely has no words

CROSS-APP CHECK. Create a file from Loopky (Settings → back up → encrypted file), then open it in pubky.app or import it into Pubky Ring. It must be accepted — if Loopky wrote Base64 text instead of raw bytes, only Loopky can read it and nothing else reports the mistake
